title: SPACE – AI-Assisted Pre/Post Command Comparison
description:
This feature introduces an AI-powered comparison engine within SPACE to analyze pre- and post-command outputs. It will:
	•	Flag any configuration removal as critical.
	•	Depend on Linked Nodes to ensure valid comparisons using a unified command set.
	•	Require a generated MOP Summary for meaningful interpretation and context. The AI agent will provide actionable insights and highlight discrepancies, enabling technicians to take corrective action before closing the change.

Requirements:
	•	Implement AI logic to compare pre- and post-command outputs.
	•	Integrate with Linked Nodes for consistent command sets.
	•	Ensure dependency on MOP Summary for contextual interpretation.
	•	Develop UI enhancements to display flagged discrepancies and severity indicators.

High-Level Design Plan:
	1	Data Preparation: Collect pre- and post-command outputs linked via Linked Nodes.
	2	AI Comparison Engine: Train and deploy models to detect discrepancies and classify severity (e.g., config removal = critical).
	3	UI Integration: Display flagged differences and recommendations in SPACE.
	4	Testing: Validate comparison accuracy, severity classification, and usability.
	5	Deployment: Roll out in phases with technician training.

Pre-requisites:
	•	Linked Nodes functionality implemented.
	•	MOP Summary generation capability available.
	•	Access to historical command outputs for model training.

Out of Scope:
	•	Automated remediation of detected discrepancies.
	•	Integration with external compliance or audit platforms.

Testing Plan:
	•	Validate AI comparison accuracy and severity classification.
	•	Test UI display and user experience.
	•	Conduct pilot with representative MOPs to measure impact.

Potential Risks:
	•	Incomplete or inconsistent command outputs affecting comparison accuracy.
	•	AI misclassification of critical changes.
	•	Resistance to AI-driven validation.
Mitigation:
	•	Standardize command sets via Linked Nodes.
	•	Use explainable AI techniques for transparency.
	•	Engage stakeholders early for trust-building and feedback.

Lead BA / E2E Owner:
Julien Eric

Stakeholder Involvement:
	•	Developers: AI comparison engine, UI integration, testing.
	•	Product Owner: Requirements, prioritization, acceptance.
	•	Change Managers & Analysts: Feedback, validation, and adoption.

Justification (PI):
By automating pre/post comparison and flagging critical discrepancies, this feature reduces preventable errors, improves compliance, and accelerates validation. These outcomes directly contribute to LFC by lowering operational costs and enhancing deployment reliability.

Post-Launch Metrics:
	•	Number of discrepancies detected and resolved.
	•	Reduction in validation-related errors.
	•	Time saved in pre/post comparison processes.
	•	User adoption and satisfaction.

Potential Benefits:
	•	Lower operational costs through early detection of critical changes.
	•	Improved compliance and validation accuracy.
	•	Faster deployment cycles and enhanced reliability.

title: Cascading Node Status Updates in SPACE
description:
This feature implements cascading node status updates in SPACE. When a parent node's status is updated, the status of its child nodes will automatically update to match. A single backend call will handle selecting all or unselecting all child nodes from the parent node. The implementation will address the behavior when a parent node is unchecked (whether child nodes should also be unchecked). The use of hotkeys or alternative selection methods will be considered.
Requirements:
	•	Implement automatic cascading updates for child nodes when a parent node's status changes.
	•	Implement a single backend call to select/unselect all child nodes from the parent node.
	•	Define the behavior when a parent node is unchecked (whether child nodes are also unchecked).
	•	Consider the implementation of hotkeys or alternative selection methods (to be determined).
High-Level Design Plan:
	•	Phase 1: Cascading Logic: Develop the logic for cascading status updates.
	•	Phase 2: Backend Call Implementation: Implement the single backend call for bulk selection/unselection.
	•	Phase 3: UI Updates: Update the UI to reflect the cascading behavior.
	•	Phase 4: Hotkey/Alternative Selection (optional): Implement hotkeys or alternative selection methods if deemed necessary.
	•	Phase 5: Testing: Thoroughly test the new functionality.
Pre-requisites:
	•	Access to the SPACE codebase.
Out of Scope: Cascading updates across non-hierarchical structures; Integration with other systems; Automated status updates based on external events.
Testing Plan:
	•	Testing of cascading status updates in various scenarios.
	•	Verification of the bulk selection/unselection functionality.
	•	Testing of the defined behavior when a parent node is unchecked.
	•	Testing of hotkeys or alternative selection methods (if implemented).
Potential Risks:
	•	Unexpected behavior due to cascading updates.
	•	Performance issues with large hierarchical structures.
	•	Mitigation: Thorough testing and efficient algorithm design will mitigate these risks.
Lead BA / E2E Owner: Refer to JIRA Feature's assignee for responsible Product Owner
Stakeholder Involvement:
	•	Developers: Design, development, and testing.
	•	Alexandre Dumouchel-Charron: Requirements validation and feedback.
Justification (PI): This feature improves the accuracy and efficiency of managing multiple nodes in SPACE, reducing manual effort and the risk of human error in updating change request statuses, ultimately leading to fewer failed changes.
Post-Launch Metrics:
	•	Frequency of use of cascading updates.
	•	Reduction in manual updates.
	•	Reduction in inconsistencies in change request status updates.
Potential Benefits:
	•	Improved accuracy of change request status updates.
	•	Reduced manual effort.
	•	Reduced risk of failed changes.

Business Justification and Value: 
By leveraging the existing BDC+BATS platform, we will prevent duplicated development efforts, delivering an estimated cost avoidance of $25,000. It also allows the team to focus on building on standard architecture rather than improving a legacy system. 
The new solution introduces automated alarm closure, which is absent in the current system. This reduces the risk of missing subsequent alerts for a recurring incident. 
This migration will mitigate some of the chronic Meraki API congestion issues. By consolidating API calls into a single, managed channel, we will reduce API rate-limit failures and ensure more reliable monitoring data. 
The current system suffers from monitoring gaps, such as missed uplink statuses and false positives alarms. Migrating to the standard BDC+BATS platform provides a stable and scalable foundation, enabling us to efficiently address these issues and build future capabilities without incurring technical debt.

Standardization & Efficiency: Reducing technical debt and simplifying operations by decommission the custom toolset. 
Enhanced Alerting Capability: Gain flexibility in setting alarm conditions, allowing Bell to respond to alarms more effectively. 
Immediate Cost Avoidance: Leverage existing functionalities from standardized toolset (e.g., automated alarm closure, API payload data collection) that would cost an estimated $25K to develop in Meraki Channel Adapter.1 
Foundation for Resolving Meraki Surveillance Issues: Lay down the backend foundation to resolve a range of Meraki alarming issues. In addition, this is a step forward to consolidate Meraki API fetching in a single toolset to mitigate current API congestion.

title: Health Check - Enhanced Script Execution History Comparison
description:
This feature enhances the HC system by adding a functionality to compare script execution results. Users will be able to select two execution history entries and generate a diff report highlighting the differences between them. Both the individual execution results and the diff report will be downloadable as text files. This will significantly improve the efficiency of troubleshooting by allowing users to quickly identify changes and pinpoint the root causes of issues.
Requirements:
	•	Implement a mechanism to select two script execution history entries for comparison.
	•	Develop an algorithm to generate a diff report highlighting the differences between the selected entries.
	•	Implement functionality to download individual execution results and the diff report as text files.
	•	Handle various data formats and potential inconsistencies in execution results.
	•	Implement appropriate error handling (e.g., if the selected entries cannot be compared).
High-Level Design Plan:
	•	Phase 1: Comparison Mechanism: Develop the algorithm to compare script execution results and generate diff reports.
	•	Phase 2: Download Functionality: Implement the functionality to download execution results and diff reports as text files.
	•	Phase 3: UI Integration: Integrate the comparison functionality into the UI.
	•	Phase 4: Error Handling: Implement robust error handling for comparison failures.
	•	Phase 5: Testing: Conduct thorough testing to validate functionality and usability.
Pre-requisites:
	•	A suitable mechanism for storing and retrieving script execution history data.
Out of Scope: Support for different file formats beyond text; Automated analysis of diff reports; Integration with other systems.
Testing Plan:
	•	Unit tests for the diff generation algorithm.
	•	Integration tests to verify interaction with the UI and data storage.
	•	User acceptance testing to validate usability and functionality.
Potential Risks:
	•	Complexity in handling various data formats and inconsistencies.
	•	Performance issues when comparing large execution results.
	•	Difficulties in generating meaningful diff reports.
	•	Mitigation: Robust error handling, efficient algorithms, and thorough testing will mitigate these risks.
Lead BA / E2E Owner: Refer to JIRA Feature's assignee for responsible Product Owner
Stakeholder Involvement:
	•	Developers: Design, development, and testing.
	•	HC users: Requirements validation and feedback.
Justification (PI): This feature significantly improves the efficiency of troubleshooting by providing a mechanism to compare script execution results and identify changes, reducing the time spent manually reviewing historical data.
Post-Launch Metrics:
	•	Frequency of comparison functionality usage.
	•	User satisfaction with the comparison feature.
Potential Benefits:
	•	Faster troubleshooting of HC issues.
	•	Improved efficiency in analyzing script execution history.
	•	Enhanced user experience.

title: Project Objective
description:
Solution will address jobs on entry and use test result, test result history, and job history to better optimize a job and perform job coordination in a more effective manner.
90 day history of job and tests will be taken into account to determine the next best action, job duration time and whether multiple technicians should be dispatched because the customer is having a re-occurring or persistent issue.
